subject.title: [Feature]: Add global --dry-run mode to prevent all tool calls from executing

question: Should OpenClaw add a trusted global agent dry-run mode as a core request-scoped security boundary, and what execution paths must be covered before exposing `openclaw agent --dry-run`?
rationale: The request is useful and vision-aligned, but the exact contract affects side-effect guarantees, concurrency, delegated/client tools, plugin hooks, and sensitive parameter logging, so automation should not pick the product/security boundary alone.

options.title: Design request-scoped core dry-run
options.body: Treat this as a core security feature and require a request-scoped implementation that proves every agent tool execution path is intercepted or explicitly excluded.

options.title: Limit to a CLI-only prototype
options.body: Accept a narrower `openclaw agent --local --dry-run` style feature first, but document that Gateway and delegated/client tool paths are out of scope.

options.title: Fold into broader safe modes
options.body: Defer this specific flag until the broader Ask/Plan/Modify workflow direction is settled in the related safe-mode discussion.

recommendation.title: Design request-scoped core dry-run
recommendation.body: Treat this as a core security feature and require a request-scoped implementation that proves every agent tool execution path is intercepted or explicitly excluded.
